title: `Pylock.select(tags=[])` still picks wheels for the running interpreter
spec:
This is the `packaging` library (Python 3, no dependencies; the code is in `src/packaging/`). Run the tests with `PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests --ignore=tests/property` (about a minute).

```python
from packaging.pylock import Pylock
h = {"sha256": "f" * 64}
url = "https://example.com/"
lock = Pylock.from_dict({"lock-version": "1.0", "created-by": "me", "packages": [{
    "name": "foo", "version": "1.0",
    "wheels": [{"name": "foo-1.0-py3-none-any.whl",
                "url": url + "foo-1.0-py3-none-any.whl", "hashes": h}],
    "sdist": {"name": "foo-1.0.tar.gz", "url": url + "foo-1.0.tar.gz", "hashes": h}}]})
[d.filename for _, d in lock.select(tags=[])]
```
Expected: `['foo-1.0.tar.gz']`. With no supported tags no wheel is compatible, so the sdist is the fallback.
Actual: `['foo-1.0-py3-none-any.whl']`. An empty list is treated as if no tags were given, so the host's tags are used.

Only `tags=None` (the default) should mean "the running interpreter's tags". For a package with no sdist, `select(tags=[])` should raise the existing `PylockSelectError` (`No wheel found matching ... and no sdist available ...`), as for any lock with no matching wheel.
acceptance: `select(tags=[])` picks the sdist in the reported example
Regression tests are added and the full test suite passes
